This application evaluates concurrent memory prediction when continuous PET and
MRI measurements are partially observed. Native study-partner ECog ratings
supply ordinal measurements; their grades are not constructed by binning imaging
or the response. Participants and observation masks are fixed before fitting.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Rmd renders serially; macOS Quartz file export avoids an optional X11 dependency.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,cache=FALSE,error=FALSE,
  dev='png',dev.args=if(Sys.info()[['sysname']]=='Darwin')list(type='quartz')else list(),dpi=130)
if(!params$action%in%c('report','plan'))stop('Render saved results or a plan; use the two method scripts to fit.')
here<-dirname(knitr::current_input(dir=TRUE));repository_dir<-normalizePath(file.path(here,'../..'))
# A local copy may live outside the checkout; the rendering caller supplies its root.
if(exists('.adni_repository_dir',inherits=TRUE))repository_dir<-get('.adni_repository_dir',inherits=TRUE)
source(file.path(repository_dir,'tools/adni.R'),local=TRUE)
list2env(as.list(adni_load_api(repository_dir)),envir=environment())
a<-get0('.adni_precomputed_analysis',inherits=TRUE)
if(is.null(a)&&params$action=='report') {
  data_dir<-if(nzchar(params$data_dir))params$data_dir else file.path(repository_dir,'data/adni')
  output_dir<-if(nzchar(params$output_dir))params$output_dir else adni_default_output('adni',params$profile,repository_dir)
  settings<-adni_settings(params$profile,params$cores,representative_fold=params$representative_fold,appendix=params$appendix)
  a<-adni_report_prepare(repository_dir,data_dir,output_dir,settings,
    if(nzchar(params$report_source))params$report_source else NULL,output_dir)
}
has_results<-!is.null(a)
table_html<-function(x,caption='',note='')cat(adni_table_html(x,caption,note),'\n\n')
```

## 1. Computation settings

- **Workflow:** `adni-eivGP.R` fits and analyzes EIV-GP; `adni-competitors.R`
  fits and analyzes UC-GP, LVGP and EzGP; `adni-report.R` assembles this Rmd from
  saved results. `--reuse-only=true` prohibits fitting in the method scripts.
- **Profiles:** ADNI `pilot` defaults to four chains, stages 1,000 and 1,500 total
  iterations, with one burn of 500. `paper` defaults to four chains, 50,000 total
  iterations and burn 5,000. Explicit numerical overrides are recorded and must
  remain compatible with saved fitting identities.
- **Sampling:** defaults are HMC at O0/O20 and elliptical slice sampling at O50.
  Core allocation changes execution concurrency, not chains, seeds or masks.
- **Inputs and outputs:** private prepared folds are read from `data/adni`
  or `--data-root`. Fits, diagnostics and empirical HTML are written to ignored
  `results/` or an external directory. Data preparation is separate from fitting.

```{r actual-settings, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(has_results) {
  table_html(data.frame(Profile=a$settings$profile,Stage=a$stage,Chains=a$numerics$chains,
    `Total iterations / chain`=a$numerics$iterations,`Burn-in / chain`=a$numerics$burn,
    `Retained / chain`=a$numerics$iterations-a$numerics$burn,check.names=FALSE),'Saved MCMC settings')
  cat('**Saved analysis selection:** folds ',paste(a$settings$folds,collapse=', '),
      '; calibration order ',paste(a$settings$cells,collapse=' / '),'. The table above reads the actual saved stage; profile defaults do not relabel historical chain budgets.\n\n',sep='')
  cat('<p><strong>Saved-result report.</strong> No optimizer, MCMC fitting or continuation is performed. A completed computation does not establish convergence.</p>\n\n')
}else cat('**Plan only:** no participant data or empirical results are embedded in this document.\n\n')
```

| Stage | Dependencies and work | Scheduling |
|---|---|---|
| Fit | Frozen folds → EIV fits and native/complete-case comparators | One public shared CPU pool; bounded resident fit objects |
| Predict | Saved fits → seeded response draws, intervals and scores | Workers borrow the same allocation |
| Functionals | Saved posterior → observable means, calibrated surfaces and target traces | Read-only, deterministic selected states and seeds |
| Report assets | Scores → tables, imputation and diagnostic figures | Cached against source and fit hashes |
| HTML | Completed saved analysis → this document | Rmd assembly; never fitting |

## 2. Data and observation design

### Notation

| Symbol | ADNI variable |
|---|---|
| \(y\) | ADNI composite memory score, ADNI_MEM; higher means better memory |
| \(u_1\) | FDG-PET MetaROI / Top50PonsVermis SUVR |
| \(u_2\) | 1,000 × (left + right hippocampal volume) / intracranial volume |
| \(c\) | Study-partner ECog item grades 1–4; each item is a separate ordinal coordinate |
| \(x\) | Age and years of education; sex is fixed within the supplied cohort |

The memory composite has a published measurement basis. PET metabolism and
hippocampal structure provide distinct imaging references, while ECog supplies
informant ratings of everyday function. This motivates concurrent prediction;
it does not establish causal effects or reliable clinical replacement of imaging.

### Ordinal measurements included in the model

```{r C-definitions, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(has_results) {
  c_table<-adni_C_dictionary(a$protocol$C_order,a$protocol$m_vec,a$metadata$C_labels)
  cat('**All ',nrow(c_table),' items below enter the model**, in the displayed C-column order. They are not averaged into a memory score or discretized from imaging.\n\n',sep='')
}else {
  example<-jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(repository_dir,'data/adni/DATASET.example.json'))
  c_table<-adni_C_dictionary(example$C_order,example$m_vec,example$C_labels)
  cat('**Default metadata example:** ',example$population,'. The private input protocol determines the actual cohort and C columns.\n\n',sep='')
}
table_html(c_table)
```

ECog-SP uses **1 = better or no change; 2 = questionable/occasionally worse;
3 = consistently a little worse; 4 = consistently much worse**. Higher grades
represent greater everyday difficulty. Code 9 (unknown) is treated as missing
before cohort construction, not as a fifth grade. Item content and grade meanings
follow the [ADNI ECog-SP field documentation](https://adni.bitbucket.io/reference/ecogsp.html).
These ratings are native ordinal observations, not imposed intervals of FDG or
hippocampal volume.

### Data-use protocols

- **OI:** all held-out participants are predicted from \((x,c)\). EIV-GP may
  use revealed training imaging; native comparators use full-training \((x,c,y)\).
- **Complete case:** comparators use calibration-training \((x,u,c,y)\) only.
  Scores share the same observed-U test participants as EIV-GP \(f(x,u)\).
- **Training-U recovery:** training \(y_i\) may inform masked U; supplied
  calibration values are excluded from error scores.
- **Prospective-U recovery:** test C is supplied without test Y. This is distinct
  from response-informed reconstruction of training U.

### Cohort construction

The prepared cohort follows ADNI quality control: qualified FDG reference
normalization, completed FreeSurfer 5.1 scans with hippocampal/overall QC passes,
finite memory and demographic measurements, and a maximum 90-day span across
matched records. One eligible matched record per participant is retained.

```{r cohort-description, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('**Population:** ',a$metadata$population,'. **Participants:** ',a$input$N,
    '; **ordinal items:** ',a$protocol$q,'.\n\n',sep='')
```

### Training and test information

Training \((x,c,y)\) is available for every training participant. O0/O20/O50
reveal zero/about 20%/50% of the **complete imaging vector**. Calibration uses
proportional native-C stratification (C1 by default), with a frozen within-stratum
random order; O20 is nested in O50. Test-U masks follow the same outcome-independent
principle. Test Y is excluded from fitting, tuning, folds and masks.

X transformations and Y normalization use training data; U anchoring uses revealed
training calibration only. Full reference U is retained for retrospective scoring
and descriptive illustrations, never passed to masked fitting inputs.

```{r design, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('**Calibration:** ',a$metadata$calibration_design,'.\n\n',sep='')
table_html(a$input$audit)
```

### EIV-GP targets and comparator scope

| Target | Evaluation and comparator scope |
|---|---|
| Held-out Y | OI scores all test participants; CC scores only the shared observed-U subset |
| Observable mean \(m(x,c)\) | EIV-GP integrates U conditional on C; native OI comparators use their recorded-input response functions |
| Calibrated response surface \(f(x,u)\) | Physical-U surfaces at O20/O50; CC comparators retain C and define a different response function |
| Training-input posterior | EIV-GP only; training Y can inform U; observed calibration is not scored as imputation |

Native items may be correlated and joint patterns sparse. Fixed-sex results do
not establish transfer to men or an independent cohort. True response functions
are unavailable; held-out-Y prediction is not a direct test of true-function recovery.

### Observed data

The following figures describe the supplied cohort once per participant. Y–U
and Y–X scatterplots follow the Ocean observed-data display. The additional C–U
boxplots show the first two C columns in fixed input order against both imaging
coordinates; all items in the preceding table remain model inputs. The illustrated
C items are not chosen by local association strength or prediction performance.

```{r observed-data, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.8}
print(a$plots$cohort)
print(a$plots$covariates)
```

```{r ordinal-imaging-data, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.5}
print(a$plots$C_U)
```

Boxes show medians and interquartile ranges, whiskers extend to 1.5 IQR, and points
show individual measured references. These are descriptive associations, not
measurement cutpoints or evidence of precise individual-U recovery.

## 3. Model fitting and numerical assessment

EIV-GP jointly models the response and ordinal measurements through latent
continuous imaging coordinates. C enters the measurement model; the response GP
uses X and U. O0 is unanchored: physical-U error scores and truth-based rotations
or rescalings are not reported. O20/O50 use observed calibration to anchor raw U.

**CORE** requires all declared core diagnostics to be finite, Rhat ≤ 1.01,
bulk ESS ≥ 400 and tail ESS ≥ 400. Dictionary occupancy is reviewed separately.
Finite diagnostic ranges do not hide undefined entries. Target diagnostics
complement the full-chain screen and cannot replace it.

```{r convergence, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
table_html(a$convergence)
```

<details><summary>Supplementary: report export status</summary>

```{r artifact-status, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(!is.null(a$artifact_manifest))table_html(a$artifact_manifest[,c('label','file','status')])
```

</details>

### Scientific-target traceplots and Monte Carlo precision

The optional `--ess-min=100` setting extends the final planned fit until monitored
scientific bulk and tail ESS both exceed 100. The default is `NULL`. Actual
per-fit iterations appear in the convergence tables; nominal stage names retain
the initially requested budget. This precision rule does not certify convergence.

```{r full-history-scientific-traces, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
full_history <- getFromNamespace('mixedgp_application_trace_report','eivGP')(
  a$output_dir, adni_path(a$output_dir,'reports','scientific-traces'))
if(length(full_history))knitr::include_graphics(full_history[grepl('[.]png$',full_history)])
```


The same representative fold is selected by configuration, never by prediction
performance. The observable-mean target uses training-defined median X, the modal
joint C profile for the other items and C1 grade 2. Imaging traces use the mean
of common-hidden training rows at that C1 grade. O0 imaging traces are in working
model units; calibrated traces are in physical units.

Function traces use conditional GP means at fixed, evenly selected retained
states; imaging traces use all retained states. Integration compares the same
fixed target with two node counts. These checks concern numerical approximation,
not proof of whole-fit stationarity or model adequacy.

```{r target-traces, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
if(!is.null(a$functionals))print(a$functionals$trace_plot)
```

```{r target-diagnostics, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(!is.null(a$functionals)) {
 table_html(adni_target_table(a),paste0('Scientific-target diagnostics: fold ',a$settings$representative_fold))
}
```

Each row assesses one plotted quantity and calibration condition. **R-hat**
compares chains; **bulk/tail ESS** measure effective sample counts; **MCSE** is
Monte Carlo error of the estimated posterior mean, not prediction error or a
posterior interval width. The mean and posterior SD describe that target's
posterior variation. These are group-mean imaging targets, not individual-U scores.
The m(x,c) target uses ADNI_MEM units. Imaging means use the unanchored model
scale at O0 and physical FDG SUVR / HIP1000/ICV units at O20/O50.
Function targets use the selected states stated above; imaging targets use full
retained chains. The table does not replace the full-fit CORE assessment.

<details><summary>Supplementary: integration check and target diagnostics across folds</summary>

Increasing latent integration nodes checks the approximation to the same fixed
observable-mean target. The difference below is the check-node estimate minus
the original estimate; it does not establish MCMC convergence.

```{r target-diagnostics-full, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(!is.null(a$functionals)) {
 table_html(adni_integration_table(a),'Latent-integration check: representative fold')
 table_html(adni_target_table(a,all_folds=TRUE),'Scientific-target diagnostics: all saved folds')
 table_html(adni_integration_table(a,all_folds=TRUE),'Latent-integration checks: all saved folds')
}
```

</details>

```{r raw-traces, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(a$functionals))print(a$functionals$raw_trace_plot)
```

```{r numerical-details, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
d<-a$method_status
if(nrow(d))table_html(d[,setdiff(names(d),'source_directory'),drop=FALSE])
if(nrow(a$stage_scores))table_html(adni_summary(a$stage_scores,c('stage','cell'),c('RMSE_SD','MAE_SD','CRPS_SD')))

 a$parameters$rhat>1.01|a$parameters$ess_bulk<400|a$parameters$ess_tail<400,,drop=FALSE]
```

## 4. Response prediction

Each table reports the mean and sample SD of fold-specific metrics. RMSE and MAE
measure point error; CRPS and interval score assess predictive distributions.
Coverage is reported with interval width. Normalization uses each full-training
Y SD before fold aggregation. Fold counts remain visible. Entries use
**mean (sample SD)**, following the Ocean report's display format.

**Bold** identifies the lowest error within the comparable information group,
including unconverged methods. `*` beside EIV-GP indicates failure of CORE; beside
a baseline it indicates at least one flagged optimizer return. Missing or
unexposed optimizer diagnostics are not reclassified as convergence.

### Ordinal-input prediction: OI

```{r oi-prediction, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div style="overflow-x:auto">',adni_metric_table(a,'OI'),'</div>\n\n')
```

### Complete-case comparison

```{r cc-prediction, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div style="overflow-x:auto">',adni_metric_table(a,'CC-known'),'</div>\n\n')
```

The known-U test subset is fixed and shared across methods. CC conclusions remain
conditional on that observation mask and calibration cohort. Mixed-input (MI)
results are retained in saved artifacts but are not displayed in this report.

## 5. Response functions

The observable mean is
\[
 m(x,c)=\int f(x,u)\,Q(du\mid c).
\]
The working input model is independent of X. Observable means integrate over
ordinally compatible U; calibrated response surfaces condition on actual U.
Neither is a causal effect.

### Observable mean m(x,c)

Slices vary the first X coordinate across its training 10th–90th percentiles and
C1 across native grades; other X coordinates use training medians and other C
items use the modal observed joint profile. Native comparators predict on exactly
the same slice. Some displayed combinations may have limited joint support.
EIV bands are pointwise posterior intervals including conditional GP uncertainty;
native lines are point predictions. These bands are not noisy-Y prediction intervals.

```{r observable-mean, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(a$functionals))print(a$functionals$mean_plot)
```

### Calibrated response function f(x,u)

Surfaces hold X at its training median and vary the imaging coordinates over
calibration-training 10th–90th percentiles. Other U coordinates, if supplied,
remain at calibration medians. Physical surfaces are shown for O20/O50 only.
The domain can differ by fold and calibration; no common-support claim is implied.

```{r calibrated-surface, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
if(!is.null(a$functionals$surface_plot))print(a$functionals$surface_plot)
```

<details><summary>Supplementary: response functions across folds</summary>

```{r all-fold-functions, eval=has_results && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=13}
if(!is.null(a$functionals))print(a$functionals$mean_all_plot)
if(!is.null(a$functionals$surface_all_plot))print(a$functionals$surface_all_plot)
```

## 6. Training-input imputation

Horizontal axes are imaging references and vertical axes are posterior means,
in full-training SD units for retrospective display. Filled points and intervals
are masked U; open points are supplied calibration values and are not scored.
Colors identify C1 grades. The dashed line is exact recovery.

```{r imputation, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(a$plots$imputation))print(a$plots$imputation)
```

```{r training-u-scores, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
table_html(adni_u_table(a$U_metrics))
if(!is.null(a$plots$common_hidden))table_html(a$plots$common_hidden)
```

The common-hidden comparison scores both calibration levels on exactly the
O50-hidden training rows. C1-mean references use revealed calibration U only,
with an overall calibration-mean fallback for unsupported grades. Reported gains
use the RMS of fold RMSEs, rather than selecting favorable participants.

### Prospective imaging recovery without test Y

```{r prospective-u, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
table_html(adni_u_table(a$prospective_metrics))
```

### Marginal distribution of hidden training inputs

The representative fold uses the same common-hidden rows under O20 and O50.
Gray histograms and rugs show their measured references; the solid curve is the
equally weighted posterior mixture using 128 saved draws per person. The dashed
curve shows posterior means and can reveal shrinkage; it is **not** the posterior
distribution of U. Axes use that fold's full-training reference SD for evaluation.
O0 is unanchored and is not overlaid with physical imaging references. Coverage
and width remain individual-interval assessments, separate from marginal spread.

```{r distributions, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
if(!is.null(a$plots$input_distribution))print(a$plots$input_distribution)
```

### Class-specific imputation calibration

Class-specific scores below summarize the saved folds. The supplementary
histograms and posterior curves use the representative fold, conditional on C1.

<details><summary>Supplementary: class-specific imputed-input distributions</summary>

```{r class-distributions, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=10}

```

</details>

```{r class-support, eval=has_results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if(!is.null(a$plots$class_table))table_html(a$plots$class_table)
if(!is.null(a$plots$support))table_html(a$plots$support)
```

ECog grades do not specify physical imaging intervals, so Ocean's category-bin
compatibility check does not apply. Instead, nonpositive physical interval
endpoints and means are counted without clipping. Counts pool repeated training
appearances across folds; they are not numbers of independent participants.

## 7. Reproducibility and references

Inputs and saved fitting identities are verified before analysis. Rebuilding
HTML never changes fitting identity, retries an optimizer or extends a chain.
Missing EIV prerequisites stop reporting; missing/flagged comparators remain
explicit. Conclusions concern this fixed cohort and recorded observation design;
independent-cohort transfer is not established.

The HTML embeds its figures. Data, fits, caches and empirical HTML remain local;
the repository supplies code, metadata examples and an empty input placeholder.
Raw imaging references are excluded from fitting wherever calibration is masked.

- Crane et al. (2012), ADNI memory composite development and validation:
  [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22782295/).
- Farias et al. (2008), Everyday Cognition scale validation:
  [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18590364/).
- Farias et al. (2013), everyday function, objective cognition and brain structure:
  [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23369894/).
